active.name: Mover
active.note: Every round it copies the step and gives it to the bird on the perch: [move | across | 1/60]. That is the whole of “moving right”.

active.name: Mover
active.note: Every round it copies the step and gives it to the bird on the perch: [move | across | -1/60]. That is the whole of “moving left”.

active.name: at the left

team.name: at the right
team.note: The edge reading says “right”: drops a x-1 on the across step to turn it round, then sends both steps.

team.name: at the near wall
team.note: The edge reading says “near”: drops a x-1 on the away step to turn it round, then sends both steps.

team.name: at the far wall
team.note: The edge reading says “far”: drops a x-1 on the away step to turn it round, then sends both steps.

team.name: moving
team.note: Any other reading: just sends both steps. It comes last so a wall gets its turn first.

active.note: Leads the team. The edge reading says “left”: drops a x-1 on the across step to turn it round, then sends both steps.

active.name: off the right

team.name: off the left
team.note: The edge reading says “left”: sends [set | across | 3/2] -- round to the right side.

team.name: moving
team.note: Any other reading: sends the step, [move | across | 1/40].

active.note: Leads the team. The edge reading says “right”: sends [set | across | -3/2], which puts my thing back at the left side.

active.name: Follower
active.note: Copies the [set | position | _] template, takes the pointer’s [across | away] off the nest, puts it in the empty hole, and gives the message to the bird on the perch. It dozes between moves.

active.name: Follower
active.note: Copies the [set | away | _] template, takes what the pointer said, moves only the AWAY of it into the hole, vacuums the rest, and sends the message: my thing follows the pointer up and down but keeps its place across.

active.name: at the left

team.name: at the right
team.note: The edge reading says “right”: drops a x-1 on the across of the speed, hands the whole speed over, then eats the reading so the team sleeps until the next wall.

team.name: at the near wall
team.note: The edge reading says “near”: drops a x-1 on the away of the speed, hands the whole speed over, then eats the reading so the team sleeps until the next wall.

team.name: at the far wall
team.note: The edge reading says “far”: drops a x-1 on the away of the speed, hands the whole speed over, then eats the reading so the team sleeps until the next wall.

team.name: setting off
team.note: The reading is “none” -- nothing has happened yet: hands the speed over once, eats the reading, and sleeps. The clock does the moving.

active.note: Leads the team. The edge reading says “left”: drops a x-1 on the across of the speed, hands the whole speed over, then eats the reading so the team sleeps until the next wall.

active.name: left

team.name: right
team.note: The key on the nest is ArrowRight: eats it and sends [move | across | 1/20].

team.name: up
team.note: The key on the nest is ArrowUp: eats it and sends [move | away | -1/20].

team.name: down
team.note: The key on the nest is ArrowDown: eats it and sends [move | away | 1/20].

team.name: any other key
team.note: Any other key: eats it, so one stray key does not stop the team.

active.note: Leads the team. The key on the nest is ArrowLeft: eats it and sends [move | across | -1/20].

active.name: contact ends

team.name: grow when bumped
team.note: Something has bumped my thing: eats the reading and sends [move | size | 1/4] -- it grows by a quarter, once per bump.

active.note: Leads the team. The touch reading says the contact has ended (“nothing”): eats it and dozes again.

active.name: contact ends

team.name: shrink when bumped
team.note: Something has bumped my thing: eats the reading and sends [move | size | -1/4] -- it shrinks by a quarter, once per bump.

active.note: Leads the team. The touch reading says the contact has ended (“nothing”): eats it and dozes again.

active.name: contact ends

team.name: ding on a hit
team.note: Something has bumped my thing: eats the reading and gives “play” to the bell’s bird -- a ding.

active.note: Leads the team. The contact has ended: eats the reading and dozes.

active.name: thing on my left

team.name: thing on my right
team.note: Something is against my right side: sets the across step to go left, then sends both steps. Flipping would not do -- half the time it turns you into the thing.

team.name: thing on my near side
team.note: Something is against my near side: sets the away step to go far, then sends both steps. Flipping would not do -- half the time it turns you into the thing.

team.name: thing on my far side
team.note: Something is against my far side: sets the away step to come near, then sends both steps. Flipping would not do -- half the time it turns you into the thing.

team.name: moving
team.note: Nothing is against me: just sends both steps.

active.note: Leads the team. Something is against my left side: sets the across step to go right, then sends both steps. Flipping would not do -- half the time it turns you into the thing.

active.name: over the limit

team.name: weighed and fine
team.note: The pans are full and the scale does not lean to the speed: under the limit, so it only clears the pans.

team.name: a speed arrives
team.note: A speed is on the channel: takes it, puts its across on one pan and the limit on the other, and vacuums the rest. Next round the lean decides.

active.note: Leads the team. The scale leans to the speed: over the limit. Sends [set | speed | [1/2 | ]] -- the across capped, the away left alone -- and clears the pans.

thing.text: send 1 to the score when hit

active.name: contact ends

team.name: one for a hit
team.note: Something has bumped my thing: eats the reading and gives a +1 to the score’s bird.

active.note: Leads the team. The contact has ended: eats the reading and dozes.

active.name: thing on my left

team.name: thing on my right
team.note: Something is against my right side: fills in the speed’s across to go left, leaves the other hole empty, hands the speed over, and eats the announcement so it sleeps until the next contact.

team.name: thing on my near side
team.note: Something is against my near side: fills in the speed’s away to go far, leaves the other hole empty, hands the speed over, and eats the announcement so it sleeps until the next contact.

team.name: thing on my far side
team.note: Something is against my far side: fills in the speed’s away to come near, leaves the other hole empty, hands the speed over, and eats the announcement so it sleeps until the next contact.

team.name: contact ends
team.note: The contact has ended: eats the announcement and sleeps again.

active.note: Leads the team. Something is against my left side: fills in the speed’s across to go right, leaves the other hole empty, hands the speed over, and eats the announcement so it sleeps until the next contact.

active.name: Wanderer
active.note: Each round, on the turn’s number: a copy of the die lands (1, 2 or 3), then the -2 (-1, 0 or 1), then the x30 (-30, 0 or 30 degrees). A copy of the turn goes to the bird on the perch, then a copy of the forward step: a yaw, then a step the way it faces.

thing.text:
THE SHELF

Twelve behaviours. Each is one
pad; its panel carries the
robots.

Set one down and press SPACE
and it does its thing to
ITSELF -- because its panel
is its own back until
somebody says otherwise.
That is the self-
demonstration, and it costs
nothing.

TO USE ONE

1. drop it on your thing
2. press SPACE on it

Nothing inside it is edited.
Only which thing its panel
is the inside of: the robots
write to the bird on the
PERCH, and that is a bird to
whatever the panel belongs to.

"." stops it. Wake Ruby and
click it and it works on
itself again.

Open its panel to read the
robots; they are ordinary
robots doing ordinary steps.

WHAT IS NOT BUILT IN

There is no move, no bounce,
no follow. There are messages
a thing already answers:

  [move | across | 1/60]
  [set | position | [x|z]]

and robots that send them.

Bouncing is three robots that
differ only in the word they
expect from the edge reading.
Flipping is a x-1 dropped on
a number.

THE SECOND SIX

and a sixteenth:
wandering -- a die of 3, a
  -2 and a x1/25 land on
  each step in turn, and a
  copy goes to the bird;
  drop it on a zoo animal

and a fifteenth:
reverse a speed on
collision -- fills in ONE
hole of the speed and
leaves the other EMPTY, so
it shares a thing with
bouncing at a speed without
the two arguing

and a fourteenth:
bouncing at a speed --
  sets a speed once, then
  sleeps until a wall, where
  one x-1 flips one number.
  The clock does the moving,
  so it never stutters and
  costs nothing between
  bounces

and a thirteenth:
following up and down --
  the pointer's AWAY only,
  so it keeps its own place
  across the table (a bat),
  and can still be pointed
  at to stop it

grow / shrink when bumped
  doze on the bump channel;
  a hit is [move | size | 1/4]

make a sound on hit
  gives "play" to its bell

reverse on collision
  sets the step away from
  what it hit, like the ball

speed limit
  weighs the speed against
  the limit on a SCALE: the
  scale is the if

send 1 to the score on hit
  a badged +1 to its bird
